en: Title: Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇatantra Author: Canonical Source: NGMPP A 136/5

Notes: This is the only manuscript known to date to contain additional chapters 26–32. However, there is almost nothing new here, as follows: Chapter 26 = *Raktayamāritantra* = *Kṛṣṇayamāritantra* 8 (the *homa* section is also found in a *Kurukullāsādhana*); Chapter 27 = *Kṛṣṇayamāritantra* 9; Chapter 28 = *Kṛṣṇayamāritantra* 10 & a series of mantras; Chapter 29 = *Kṛṣṇayamāritantra* 11; Chapter 30 = *Kṛṣṇayamāritantra* 12; Chapter 31 = *Kṛṣṇayamāritantra* 13; Chapter 32 = *Kṛṣṇayamāritantra* 14.
Then the Blessed One said:
Listen, O Vajradhara King! Through the application of the protection wheel, he spoke to Nintikūti, the leader of the obstructors, impediments, and the wicked.
I am King Khaḍgadhara; through the application of the protection-wheel, I shatter that which is born of the three bodies with my sword, which blazes like fire.
O Goddess, you are the witness for all those who follow the Buddhas;
O Yamaghni, as the master of the mandala, I shall draw the mandala.
Having bound his mouth with a cloth from Kāśī, he should stand at the door of the maṇḍala hall and say, "Who are you, sir? to which he should reply, "I am Subhaga."
Having placed the curtain inside, the wise disciple should pray to the Guru with devotion for the sake of initiation;
having recited [the request] three times, he should entreat him again.
Just as the Buddhas [bestowed] the great dharmas through the consecration of Vajrasattva,
may he also grant me this boon for the sake of my protection.
The disciple should respectfully offer songs, instrumental music, worship, as well as water for honor and water for the feet; or he should cause a hymn of praise to be performed there.
Then one should recite the mantra of emptiness for Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa:
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the wisdom of emptiness.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the perfectly pure dharmadhātu.
Oṃ, homage be to Kṛṣṇācala; crush all Māras, hūṃ phaṭ!
The Blessed One said:
Now I shall explain the fire-oblation (homa) according to its various classifications, such as the pacifying rite (śāntika) and others,
by means of which oblation success may be attained that accomplishes all ritual actions.
In rites for pacification, with a peaceful mind; in rites for enrichment, with a nourishing intention; in rites for subjugation, with a longing mind; but in rites for killing, with a distressed mind.
For pacification, the external form is circular; for enrichment, it is likewise;
for subjugation, it is called the half-moon; and for killing, it is like the element of space.
For pacification, the length should be one cubit; likewise, for nourishment, it should be two cubits.
As it is for nourishment, so it is for subjugation; for killing, it should be twenty finger-breadths.
One should pierce to half a cubit for pacification, but to one full cubit for nourishment;
the thumb-breadth [measurement] is for killing, and as it is for nourishment, so it is for subjugation.
On the new moon day, one should perform the *sāntika* (pacifying) fire sacrifice; on the full moon day, the *pauṣṭika* (prosperity-inducing);
on the fourteenth day for malevolent rites (*abhicāra*); and on the eighth day for the rite of subjugation (*vaśya*).
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, the Chapter on Fire Offerings (Homa), in the *Śrīcaṇḍamahāroṣaṇatantra*, known as the *Ekallavīra*.
Then the Blessed One said:
Having taken clay from the ocean, one should fashion a single Nāga;
having placed the syllable *oṃ phuṃ* upon its heart, one should recite the mantra beginning with *hrīṃḥ ṣṭyā*.
During a time of drought, one should cause rain to fall by performing ten thousand recitations;
one should mix the flesh of a black snake with nimba leaves.
Having made a wick with that very [substance], the practitioner should cast it into the ocean;
by reciting the mantra ten thousand times, the supreme stalling of the waves is achieved.

Taking one hundred seeds of *caṇḍa* mixed with black gram and rice, one should perform a fire oblation (*homa*) after reciting [the mantra] eight hundred thousand times; by this very act, let it be seen.
The practitioner, observing the vow, should have a doll fashioned from the ashes of a cremation ground using collyrium;
by anointing it with the juice of *unmatta* for ten thousand times, [the target] becomes infatuated.
By reciting the mantra four hundred thousand times with a collection of white mustard seeds (siddhārtha), one should perform the rite of awakening the sleeping; there is no doubt that he will live.
Now I shall further explain another method, the great sādhana of the vetāla,
which is divine, brings about all accomplishments, and effects various tasks.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, the Chapter on Bhīma’s Recollection, in the Śrīcaṇḍamahāroṣaṇatantra known as the Ekallavīra.
Then the Blessed One said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain what is called Caṇḍaroṣaṇa:
one should take a tree-hanging [corpse] that is uninjured, free of wounds, and auspicious.
One should visualize the four wrathful deities situated in the center of a solar mandala;
one should visualize the four goddesses situated in the center of a clear mandala.
% *Kṛtyātantra*, chapter 10 ends here.
Then the Blessed One, having entered the meditative absorption named "Victory over All Māras," uttered this mantra and said:
oṃ vighnāntakṛt vajrakrodha hayagrīva hūru 2 hūṃ phaṭ |
Oṃ caṇḍamahāroṣaṇāya trāṃ hāṃ māṃ hāṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ namaḥ kṛṣṇācalāya sarvamāra jambhaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ | Oṃ namaḥ śvetācalāya sarvaduṣṭa mohaya 2 hūṃ phaṭ |
Oṃ, homage to Pītācala, destroyer of all fears! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ, homage to Raktācala, bind the mouths of all enemies! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, homage to Śyāmācala, destroyer of the fear of all spirits! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa! Strike, strike! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Grind, grind! O infallible Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa, [destroy] all enemies! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, the Chapter on the Recollection of the Sadhana, in the glorious Caṇḍamahāroṣaṇa Tantra known as the Ekallavīra.
Then the Blessed One said: "Having seen the world overcome by hatred, the Blessed One, out of compassion, brought about the state of Dveṣavajrī, which brings about the destruction of all hatred."
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, on the Conduct and Observances, in the *Śrīcaṇḍamahāroṣaṇatantra* known as the *Ekallavīra*.

Then the Blessed One, the Great Being, having entered the meditative absorption of the form of Vajracarcikā, having entered the meditative absorption of the form of Vajravārāhī, having entered the meditative absorption of the form of Sarasvatī, and having entered the meditative absorption of the form of Gaurī, uttered this song of worship:
Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, the special chapter on all the narratives, in the *Śrīcaṇḍamahāroṣaṇatantra* known as the *Ekallavīra*.
Then the Blessed One said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain how many are those who perform evil deeds;
indeed, one cuts them away with the blade [of wisdom] by severing hair, afflictions, and the like.
